analyst_view.overall: Napoli (10th, 15 points, one win in five and only five wins in all competitions since Allegri replaced Conte) host Torino (11th, 14 points, one point behind) three days before a Champions League game against Manchester City. Meret is out, so Milinkovic-Savic starts in goal, and Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Badiashile, Alisson Santos and Buongiorno are missing (most counted by the numbers); Neres, Favasuli and Marianucci are available again. Saturday's previews still expect De Bruyne, Napoli's top scorer, to start on the bench with Gilmour alongside McTominay, so he is fresh for City, while Hojlund, Vergara and Politano lead the attack. Torino under Abate get Mandragora back; Vlasic has a minor thigh strain (one preview has Casadei starting instead, another expects Vlasic to play) and wing-backs Belghali, Rodriguez and Fortini carry knocks, with Adams and Simeone up front. Referee Antonio Rapuano (5.1 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already cut for Lobotka and Di Lorenzo and raised for Meret's absence and Napoli's leaky defence (14 conceded in six). Saturday's previews still have De Bruyne, Napoli's top scorer, on the bench before City, and Torino may lack Vlasic's creativity; a mild lean down to about 2.6, since De Bruyne should still come on.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Napoli have won few corners lately (21 in six) while Torino concede plenty, and Torino's 3-5-2 with wing-backs is their usual shape even if Belghali or Rodriguez miss out; a De Bruyne rest affects set-piece delivery more than how often corners come, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add Rapuano's high rate (+32%). Both sides have been fairly calm lately, no suspensions are reported and the previews raise no rivalry angle, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, already lifted for Torino's shooting against a Napoli side that has allowed many chances (103 shots in six). Without De Bruyne from the start Napoli lose some long-range shooting, but Gilmour and McTominay still push forward and Napoli must chase a win at home, so I stay at about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already raised for Napoli's sharp recent shooting (37 on target in six). De Bruyne, Napoli's best finisher this season, is expected on the bench and Vlasic is a doubt for Torino, which takes a little quality off both attacks; a small trim to about 8.5.
